4º de Primaria · Inglés

Reading and writing a short story

Ficha para imprimir
123456
1

Pregunta de arranquePiensa 30 segundos antes de seguir

Casi todos los cuentos que conoces empiezan igual: «Érase una vez…». ¿Sabes cómo empiezan los cuentos en inglés?

Escribe o di en voz alta tu respuesta. Después .

Con Once upon a time… Y como en español, los cuentos tienen tres partes: beginning (principio), middle (nudo, con un problema) y end (desenlace). Si conoces este esquema, ¡puedes leer y escribir tus propios cuentos en inglés!

2

Aprende9 bloques cortos

What is a story?

A story tells us about things that happen to some characters in a place. Stories can be real or invented, funny or scary, about animals, kids, monsters or robots. Fairy tales, fables and comics are all kinds of stories.

Every good story has three ingredients: who (the characters), where and when (the setting) and what happens (the plot). En castellano: story es «cuento» o «historia»; tale también es cuento, y fairy tale es un cuento de hadas.

Characters and setting

The characters are the people or animals in the story. The main character (protagonista) is the most important one. We describe characters with adjectives: brave (valiente), shy (tímido), clever (listo), kind (amable), naughty (travieso), grumpy (gruñón).

The setting is where and when the story happens: in a dark forest, in a castle, at school, on a spaceship, a long time ago, last summer… Consejo: un buen escenario ayuda al lector a imaginar la historia.

Beginning, middle and end

Stories have three parts. In the beginning we meet the characters and the setting: «Once upon a time, there was a little robot called Bip». In the middle there is a problem: «One day, Bip lost his battery». In the end the problem is solved: «Finally, his friend found it and Bip was happy again».

En castellano: es el mismo esquema que en Lengua: planteamiento, nudo y desenlace. Sin problema no hay historia: ¡algo tiene que salir mal para que la aventura sea interesante!

Linking words

Linking words help us tell the events in order. To start: Once upon a time (érase una vez), One day (un día), Long ago (hace mucho tiempo). To continue: Then (luego), Next, After that. For a surprise: Suddenly (de repente).

To finish: In the end, Finally (al final) and The end (fin). Consejo: Suddenly es la palabra mágica para presentar el problema: «Suddenly, a big storm started…». ¡Engancha al lector!

Stories in the past

Most stories are told in the past. You don't need to know all the past tenses yet, but these verbs appear in almost every story: was / were (era, estaba), there was (había), lived (vivía), wanted (quería), went (fue), saw (vio), said (dijo), found (encontró), had (tenía).

Example: «Once upon a time, there was a girl who lived near the sea. One day she went to the beach and saw a bottle». Read them as words and you'll understand the story perfectly.

Reading: The Little Cloud

Read this story: «Once upon a time, there was a little cloud called Nimbo. He lived high in the sky with his family. Nimbo was very shy. The other clouds made big storms, but he only made a tiny drop of rain. One day, he saw a small village with a dry garden. The flowers were sad and brown. Suddenly, Nimbo had an idea. He said: "I can help!". He cried and cried, very softly. Finally, the flowers opened and the children danced in the rain. Nimbo wasn't shy any more. The end.»

Vídeo: The Wind and the Sun · The Fable Cottage (YouTube) · 5,1 millones de visualizaciones

Understanding the story

Let's analyse «The Little Cloud». Characters: Nimbo (the main character), his family, the flowers and the children. Setting: the sky and a small village. Beginning: Nimbo is a shy little cloud. Problem: the garden is dry and the flowers are sad. End: Nimbo makes gentle rain and the flowers open.

What's the message of the story? Maybe: «Small things can help a lot» or «Everyone is good at something». Pregunta: ¿qué palabra presenta la idea de Nimbo? (Suddenly).

Planning your own story

Before writing, make a story map (esquema). Answer these questions: Who is the main character? What is he/she like? Where does the story happen? What is the problem? How is it solved?

Ideas: a dragon who is afraid of fire, a cat who wants to be an astronaut, a pencil that draws by itself, a girl who finds a secret door in the library. Consejo: elige una sola idea y un solo problema. Los mejores cuentos cortos son sencillos.

Writing your story

Now write your story in three paragraphs, about 60 to 80 words. Paragraph 1: «Once upon a time, there was… He/She lived in…». Paragraph 2: «One day… Suddenly…». Paragraph 3: «Finally… The end».

Check your work with this list: Does it have a title? Are there capital letters at the start of sentences and for names? Did you use full stops (.)? Did you use at least three linking words? Then illustrate it and read it aloud to a younger class. ¡Ya eres escritor en inglés!

Lo hacemos juntos

Put the sentences in order: «Finally, the cat came home.» «One day, the cat got lost.» «Once upon a time, there was a cat called Coco.»

  1. El principio empieza con Once upon a time.
  2. El problema llega con One day.
  3. El final, con Finally.

Resultado: Once upon a time… → One day… → Finally…

Find the problem: «Leo wanted to fly his kite. Suddenly, the kite got stuck in a tree.»

  1. Busca la palabra Suddenly.
  2. Lo que sale mal es el problema.

Resultado: The kite got stuck in a tree.

Describe a character with two adjectives.

  1. Elige un personaje: a dragon.
  2. Adjetivos: brave, kind.

Resultado: The dragon was brave and kind.

Errores típicos

  • Escribir un cuento sin problema: sin nudo, no pasa nada interesante.
  • Olvidar las mayúsculas en los nombres: «nimbo» → «Nimbo».
  • Usar solo «and then» todo el rato: alterna then, after that, suddenly, finally.
  • Escribir todo en un solo párrafo: separa principio, nudo y final.
  • Traducir «érase una vez» palabra por palabra: es «Once upon a time».

Ejercicios

Hazlos en tu cuaderno y después abre la solución.

  1. How do stories start in English?

    Ver solución
    Once upon a time…

  2. Translate: personaje, escenario, problema.

    Ver solución
    character, setting, problem.

  3. What are the three parts of a story?

    Ver solución
    Beginning, middle and end.

  4. Which linking word introduces a surprise?

    Ver solución
    Suddenly.

  5. Translate: valiente, tímido, travieso.

    Ver solución
    brave, shy, naughty.

  6. Who is the main character in «The Little Cloud»?

    Ver solución
    Nimbo, a little cloud.

  7. What is the problem in «The Little Cloud»?

    Ver solución
    The garden is dry and the flowers are sad.

  8. Translate: «Había un perro que vivía en un castillo.»

    Ver solución
    There was a dog who lived in a castle.

  9. Write a beginning for a story about a robot.

    Ver solución
    Model answer: Once upon a time, there was a small robot called Zap. He lived in a big city.

  10. Write an ending with «Finally».

    Ver solución
    Model answer: Finally, Zap found his friends and they had a party. The end.

Para familias

  • Leed juntos un cuento corto en inglés y buscad el principio, el problema y el final.
  • Inventad entre todos un cuento: cada uno añade una frase empezando por un conector.
  • Repasad juntos las tarjetas del paso 6 dos minutos al día durante una semana.

Para profesores

Saberes: Comprensión de textos narrativos breves; estructura del cuento; conectores temporales; producción escrita guiada de un relato (Lengua Extranjera) (RD 157/2022, segundo ciclo de Primaria).

  • Cuento colectivo: cada alumno añade una frase con un conector.
  • Esquema «story map» antes de escribir.
  • Lectura de los cuentos de la clase a un curso más pequeño.

Qué vas a aprender

  • Recognise the parts of a story: beginning, middle and end
  • Identify characters, setting and problem
  • Use linking words: once upon a time, one day, suddenly, finally
  • Plan and write a short story of your own
